summary: Rewrites the AFAW auditor spec (duo/custom-agent.md) with the 22 read tools of the Web UI and two optional note tools, states that find_files, grep, read_file, read_files, list_dir and run_command are IDE-only and not used, lists the tools forbidden for the agent, and fixes the system prompt: findings go in the chat, or as a merge request note when the comment tools are selected. Adds the AFAW planner spec (duo/custom-planner.md, 9 tools, its own system prompt). scripts/check_duo_config.py now enforces the allow list of each agent, the forbidden list and the IDE-only list, and requires both spec files; its tests were written first and failed on the old code. Verified on docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/agents/tools on 2026-10-25: all 44 names exist, six are IDE-only; the page marks no tool as read or write, so that classification and the forbidden list are the project's. docs/duo.md records the tool tables and two open points: whether the Developer Flow sandbox provides read_file and grep for the workspace subagent, and how human_only_files sees a merge request attributed to the person who triggered a flow. Follow-up after the human created the AFAW auditor in the UI: the allow list gains four documented read tools (get_commit_comments, get_failing_bridge_jobs, get_issue_note, gitlab_issue_search), the spec carries the prompt of the created agent with rule 2 changed so that it does not claim to run tests, and get_job, get_pipeline and get_merge_request_conflicts stay rejected as unknown because the tools page (checked 2026-10-25) does not list them.
